# Pilot lab fixtures

Answers Tally gave on 2026-10-09 on the synthetic company `BRIDGE PILOT LAB` (TallyPrime 7.1
Silver, licensed mode), sent by an outside contributor from a machine of their own, one request at a
time, each answer written straight to a file with `curl.exe -o` and never piped. The company was
the only one loaded. The contributor published the answers on the branch `lab/1342-capture-answers` (commit
`4bceb5d0`) with a hash table; each file here is byte-equal to the file there and its SHA-256
equals the one in that table.

The data is synthetic: the company, its GSTIN (of the synthetic family the fixtures may carry)
and its ledgers were made for this measurement. One book, one release, one day.

| Fixture | Bytes | SHA-256 | What it is | Request |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| `pilot-lab-tax-units-typed-request.utf8.xml` | 11,152 | `f66ed7c325edc01e6d5d627e6c3490b6f7c3edf573ddf670d936e0783cbb9e40` | the company's tax units, all fields, read after the registration was entered and before any voucher was keyed: the Default Tax Unit and one GST registration, `Rajasthan Registration`, with one dated row from 2026-04-01 (Regular, not inactive); UTF-8 with CRLF line ends, as received; Tally's `&#4;` references as received | typed by hand from the text in the request list of #1342 (`b-taxunit.xml`, 426 bytes, SHA-256 `e5bbb2ab3e16838d8cb3a39c48d0d5683d5a8d565e099783af0c240d58d30081`, sent as UTF-8): the same collection, type and `NATIVEMETHOD *` as `render_company_registration_request`, under another collection name and in UTF-8, where the code sends UTF-16. The code's own request was answered on 9 Oct 2026 (`pilot-lab-tax-units.utf16le.xml`, below). |

## The invoice round (2026-10-09)

The one-invoice round of #1342, sent by the same contributor on the same company, the same way: one request at a time, each answer written straight to a file with `curl.exe -o`. The answers are on `lab/1342-capture-answers` (the third-round reads in `fixed3/` at commit `0b85a64c`, the invoice round in `post/` at commit `01cbee0b`); each file here is byte-equal to the file there, and its SHA-256 equals the one in that branch's hash table. The book is the one the third-round reads describe: ten keyed vouchers dated 2026-08-01, then `BP/26-27/0010`, imported once from `pilot-lab-invoice-post-request.utf16le.xml`, which ComplyEaze Bridge's own build rendered from these answers (REMOTEID `00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000777`).

## The parent-filter round (2026-10-10, #1331)

Four read-only requests sent by the same contributor on the same company, the same way (one at a time, each answer written straight to a file with `curl.exe -o`, once each; curl exit 0 and HTTP 200 for all). The requests are on `lab/1331-capture-requests` (commit `5876c342`), the answers on `lab/1331-capture-answers` (commit `b5c0ff86`); each file here is byte-equal to the file there and its SHA-256 equals the one in that branch's hash table. The book is the one after the later #1342 rounds: fifteen ledgers, so these answers are not paired with the invoice round's answers above, which describe eleven. `pilot-lab-ledger-catalogue-v2-10oct` and the two scoped answers are one coherent set: the catalogue, and the rates request filtered to the parents of the lab invoices' legs.
